transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-29 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Themis - Head of ML), Carlos Vega (Themis - Infra), Marta Olsen (Themis - Product)

Summary:
Quick sync on pilot throughput numbers after last weekend's ramp. Focus: continuous batching tuning, concurrency targets per shard, queueing/backpressure behavior, and plan for a weekend replay. Agreed to run kernel-level profiler and share traces.

Topics:
- Weekend ramp outcomes and anomalies
- Batching window and latency tail tradeoffs
- Concurrency ceilings per-GPU vs per-model-instance
- Queue depth shaping and backpressure responses
- Next steps and owners for traces / replays

Action items (recorded in transcript too):
- Samir: share updated batching config and sample traces
- Jordan: run profiler and produce flame graphs
- Carlos: provide realistic QPS pattern for replay

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir: ok, let's get started. Thanks everyone for joining, we have 45 minutes, I know you all are squeezed so we'll go straight into the weekend numbers.
[00:18] Priya: cool, thanks. we looked at the dashboard this morning, saw a big spike around 03:10 UTC, it looks like concurrency hit 28 on a shard and latency spiked to 620 ms p95, which is odd because our expectations were around 380.
[00:36] Jordan: yeah, that's what the SE noticed — there's a pattern where continuous batching window widened under that burst, so more tokens got accumulated and the per-request wait increased. Could be queueing at the request router or backpressure from the KV cache refill.
[00:55] Carlos: we also saw a few dropped connections from the load balancer but that might be unrelated, we had a node OOM earlier in the day, gc churn maybe.
[01:12] Samir: ok, let's separate out the signals. Jordan, can you summarize the batching config we had during the ramp?
[01:24] Jordan: Sure — right now pilot uses continuous batching with a 12 ms max window and adaptive join on the request size. We increased the batch cap to 64 tokens per batch for longer seqs, concurrency target per-instance set to 24. During the burst we allowed burst-concurrency to scale to 32 which pushed GPU to 96% util. That seems to magnify the queueing tail.
[01:48] Priya: so raising the cap helped throughput but killed tail latencies. We're trying to understand acceptable SLOs: product wants sub-500 ms p95 for interactive flows.
[02:02] Marta: yes product says p95 < 500ms, p99 < 900ms. We're fine with some cost increase for average throughput but not for tail spikes.
[02:16] Jordan: couple quick notes — the runtime's dynamic batching uses a token-length histogram to shape batches, but with this traffic shape the histogram shifts and we get few large batches that block small fast requests. There is an option to do prioritized batching (small-first), but that burns some kernels as they fragment.
[02:37] Carlos: hmm, prioritized small-first might help user-facing latency, what's the CPU cost there? We have limited headroom on the router nodes.
[02:46] Samir: good question. Jordan, any concrete numbers?
[02:50] Jordan: ballpark: prioritized batching adds around 8-12% CPU at the router and can reduce p95 by 20-30% in our test harness, but it can reduce overall throughput by 6-10% if tokens distribution shifts.
[03:08] Priya: that sounds like a tradeoff we can accept for now, maybe enable prioritized batching only during interactive endpoints. We have separate routes for long-form generation.
[03:20] Samir: that's reasonable. Another knob is concurrency ceilings per-GPU; we had 24 set but we saw the shard go to 32 under burst. If we hard cap at 28 we might avoid long queue buildup at the cost of rejecting some concurrent requests or falling back to a cheaper model.
[03:40] Marta: what's the fallback behavior look like — do we get graceful fallback to a lighter quantized model or do requests get queued indefinitely?
[03:48] Jordan: in the pilot config we have model-fallback to a 4-bit quant variant and region fallback disabled. Fallback currently has a small cold-start penalty for the quant model (warmup ~30ms), but it's usually faster overall under heavy load.
[04:04] Carlos: we worry about quality regression with quant model for our classification task — Priya, any tolerance?
[04:12] Priya: we ran evals earlier, the quant model dropped F1 by about 0.8 points on our sensitive categories, not ideal but maybe acceptable for degraded mode if we mark the responses.
[04:27] Samir: ok put that on the decision tree: if p95 > 700ms for two consecutive windows, route to quant fallback for non-critical endpoints.
[04:37] Jordan: back to batching — we also saw that the KV cache refill during the burst had a bursty I/O pattern; that created short stalls on the GPU side when a hot prefix wasn't in cache. The runtime falls back to the model step to rebuild KV which adds 80-120ms occasionally.
[04:56] Priya: is there a configurable warm cache strategy? like prefetching top-k prefixes per user cohort?
[05:04] Jordan: yes, there's a prefix prefetch policy we can tune. It costs some memory but reduces those rebuild stalls. For Themis traffic shape, prefetch top-50 prefixes per shard cut the KV miss penalty in half in our lab tests.
[05:20] Marta: memory is okay, we have slack on Dedicated nodes, but we need to see exact numbers.
[05:27] Samir: Jordan, can you prepare a comparison: current vs prioritized batching vs prioritized+prefetch, include CPU and memory numbers and p95/p99 effects?
[05:39] Jordan: yep, I can do that — I'll run the three profiles with weekend traffic replay and attach logs.
[05:44] Carlos: about the weekend replay, we can extract the QPS envelope and supply a synthetic workload; we'll include numpy-style variance so it's not a static replay.
[05:54] Samir: perfect, please share by Thursday.
[06:00] Priya: one more oddity — the tracer shows occasional latency cliffs at ~13:40 UTC where requests waited ~300ms before entering the batch process. Looks like the router queueing timer misfired.
[06:14] Jordan: could be a timer resolution issue when we had GC spikes on the router. We saw a JVM stop-the-world earlier that day at 13:38 in the trace.
[06:25] Marta: is Redwood using a non-blocking router now? I remember earlier pilot baseline used blocking I/O.
[06:32] Samir: current pilot uses the async router path, but some older shards still have the blocking shim enabled for compatibility. That mismatch can create jitter.
[06:43] Carlos: can we ensure all shards are on the async path before next ramp? else we get mixed behavior.
[06:49] Samir: yes, we'll audit and flip the remaining shims. Jordan will coordinate.
[06:55] Jordan: noted. I'll add a checklist and a deploy window.
[07:02] Priya: thank you. Also curious about concurrency shaping — is there an SLO-aware admission controller that can reject/queue selectively?
[07:11] Jordan: there is an admission policy DSL we can use to prioritize interactive endpoints and throttle background requests. It's a rule engine, we can add thresholds per-route.
[07:22] Samir: maybe we use route labels: interactive=true then give those routes lower batching window and lower queue tolerance.
[07:31] Marta: one operational ask: when you flip configs, can you notify via the slack pilot channel and pin the exact git diff? We need audit for compliance.
[07:40] Samir: yes, we'll push a PR and tag it in #pilot-themis.
[07:44] Carlos: regarding cost, we saw cost per 1M tokens increased by 12% when we allowed burst concurrency. Any knobs to reduce cost without hurting p95 too much?
[07:56] Jordan: yes — quantize at compile-time for warm paths, reduce max batch cap for long-seq routes, and enable cache sharing across shards for hot prefixes. Each has tradeoffs.
[08:08] Priya: cache sharing sounds promising; less duplication could reduce memory and speed up warms.
[08:15] Jordan: caveat: cross-shard sharing increases network calls for keys not local, small latency penalty but overall better hit rate. We can simulate.
[08:24] Samir: ok, let's prioritize experiments: 1) prioritized batching for interactive routes, 2) prefix prefetch top-50, 3) adjust concurrency cap to 28 and enable quant fallback on degradation, 4) test cache-sharing in sim. Jordan will run simulations and flamegraphs, Carlos will supply QPS; Samir to share configs and traces.
[08:46] Marta: sounds like plan. Question: do you recommend adjusting autoscaling policy for the pilot? We had relatively slow_scale_up which might be part of the tail issue.
[08:57] Jordan: yes, changing the scale policy to be more aggressive on short bursts helps if you can tolerate some brief overprovisioning. A warm-burst pool approach (reserve 10% capacity for burst) performed well in our benchmarks.
[09:11] Carlos: we can try warm-burst pool but need to watch monthly committed spend. We'll model costs.
[09:18] Priya: can you include cost delta in the experiment outputs? we need to make a tradeoff doc for exec.
[09:24] Samir: yes will include cost delta per experiment.
[09:28] Jordan: I'll plan profiling runs tonight in the staging mirror and post flamegraphs and a short write-up.
[09:36] Samir: ok, logistics — Jordan will attach artifacts to the Asana task; Samir will send updated batching config and the pilot dashboard export (CSV + traces). Carlos will produce the synthetic QPS file. We reconvene next Tuesday same time.
[09:50] Priya: quick Q: backups for the KV cache — we had a suggestion to persist hot prefixes to SSD to avoid full rebuilds after evictions, is that feasible in Dedicated?
[10:03] Jordan: yes, we have an optional on-disk prefix hotstore. It increases disk I/O but drops rebuilds. For Dedicated we can enable an SSD-backed cache; I'd quantify the I/O cost.
[10:15] Marta: let's try in sim first.
[10:18] Samir: good. Anything else?
[10:21] Priya: no, thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround on artifacts.
[10:25] Carlos: thanks.
[10:27] Samir: great, I'll send notes and the batching diff by tomorrow morning. Thanks everyone.

Recap / Agreed next steps:
- Jordan: prioritized batching + prefetch sim runs, kernel profiler + flamegraphs, simulate cache-sharing (due 2027-04-05)
- Samir: export dashboard, sample traces, and push batching config PR (due 2027-04-01)
- Carlos: produce realistic QPS replay file (due 2027-04-03)
- Team: reconvene Tuesday 2027-04-05 for results review
